text:
Only one earlier Joad matter is in the stored knowledge: *Estate of Sven Lindqvist v. Joad Axle Works*, Tamarack County Superior No. TC-23-0459. I haven't used the firm's other client matters, because that material belongs to other clients and shouldn't inform your work for Joad.

**Test results**
- **FT-77 fatigue series (2017):** Four specimens reached runout and one failed at 82% of runout. Plaintiff will use the failed specimen to argue an inadequate safety margin. This series is central to discovery, and Joad treats it as highly sensitive.
- **Joad's own metallurgist (preliminary):** The final overload zone is large, and the fracture surface shows heavy smearing from post-separation contact. Both findings are consistent with an impact failure.
- **Recorder data:** The electronic data recorder read 41 mph on a ramp posted at 35 mph. This supports comparative fault and an alternative cause.

**Metallurgical findings**
- **Fracture location:** The left spindle of the JX-9 tandem drive axle separated at the inboard bearing shoulder.
- **Plaintiff's theory:** Their metallurgist, Dr. Fenwick Ashdown, will argue that beach marks show months of fatigue progression, so the spindle was cracked before June 9, 2022.
- **Adverse fact:** A privileged post-accident metallurgical review found a machining tool mark at the fracture origin. The reviewer could not rule it out as the initiation point. It is withheld as work product and has not been produced. Be careful about who sees it and don't reference it outside the privileged circle.
- **Chain of custody:** The spindle sat eight months in a yard before it was moved. That raises spoliation and smearing questions.

**Witnesses**
- **Bertil Oakhurst**, Joad's chief axle engineer, ran the 2017 test program and will be a central witness. He is not to be put forward for testimony until the firm and General Counsel Evander Thorsby have discussed it.
- **Hollis Pruett**, a former test technician who left in 2019, carried out the FT-77 testing. Plaintiff may depose him.
- **Dr. Fenwick Ashdown** is plaintiff's metallurgist.
- **Dr. Lorraine Pettibone** is plaintiff's reconstructionist. She will say the speed was legal and the only reasonable explanation for the loss of control is axle failure.
- **Octavia Brandvold** is plaintiff's counsel.
- **Dr. Raul Esquivel** (axle design and testing) and **Dr. Mathilde Grosvenor** (standards subcommittee chair) are the proposed defense experts. Neither should be engaged until the client has reviewed and approved them.
- **Perpetua Wallace**, the Cobaltridge Indemnity claims handler, should be copied on anything bearing on coverage.

**Other points to be ready for**
- **Supplier change:** Joad changed its spindle forging supplier in 2020 after an internal audit. The client wants the reason kept within the case team. Understand the Corbelmark supplier-qualification program before any supplier discussion.
- **Sibling models:** Discovery was limited to JX-9 spindle reports and JX-9 wheel-end bearing-shoulder reports. The JX-7 and JX-11 were excluded because they have different spindle geometry, unless discovery shows a shared part.
- **Redfern records:** The last three bearing services are likely to cut both ways. A missed service helps the maintenance defense, but plaintiff may blame Joad's manual.

**Caveats**
- The only Answer in the file is a July 14, 2023 draft that pleads lack of knowledge about speed. Confirm whether it was amended or filed as drafted.
- The sequence question (cracked before the rollover or broken in it) is genuinely contested. The assessments above are preliminary.
- All communications go through Thorsby. Don't contact Joad engineers directly.
